Calculated in the source sheet as `=IFS(B1="Base model",470, B1="Conservative",568, B1="Moderate",568, B1="Optimistic",568)`; kept as a fixed number here (IFS()).

  'Supply Side Cash (Malawi)'!B1="Base model", 1%,

)`; kept as a fixed number here (IFS()).

rows.label: Total size of transfer per household (nominal USD) (Malawi)
rows.explainer:
Calculated in the source sheet as `=IFS(
  $B$1="Base model", 1000,
  $B$1="Conservative", 778,
  $B$1="Moderate", 778,
  $B$1="Optimistic", 778
)`; kept as a fixed number here (IFS()).

Assumes $778 average transfer size as the weighted average across our 2 transfer size bins ($1,000 and $500), which will be assigned based on observable characteristics as a proxy for capital constraints. Default to GD's moderate scenario "MW [Malawi] is ~$550 per person.” GiveDirectly, comments on a draft of the associated write-up, October 2, 2024.

For a two-person household this figure would then be ~$1,100. We deflate this to $1,000 to account for single person households.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
